p2-start.say: All right? Remember, you have one to two minutes for this, so don't worry if I stop you. I'll tell you when the time is up. Can you start speaking now, please?

end.say: Thank you. That is the end of the Speaking test.

questions.text: How long have you lived in your present home?
questions.say: Good evening. My name is Lewis, and I'm your examiner today. This is the Speaking test. In this first part, I'd like to ask you some questions about yourself. Let's talk about your home. How long have you lived in your present home?

questions.text: Is your home quiet or noisy?
questions.say: Is your home quiet or noisy?

questions.text: How long does it take you to get from your home to the city centre?
questions.say: How long does it take you to get from your home to the city centre?

questions.text: Do you prefer living alone or with other people?
questions.say: Do you prefer living alone or with other people?
Now let's move on to talk about money. Do you usually carry cash?

questions.text: Do you prefer paying by card or with cash?
questions.say: Do you prefer paying by card or with cash?

questions.text: Did you get pocket money as a child?
questions.say: Did you get pocket money as a child?
Now let's move on to talk about shopping centres. Do you like shopping centres?

questions.text: How often do you go to one?
questions.say: How often do you go to one?

questions.text: What do you usually do there apart from shopping?
questions.say: What do you usually do there apart from shopping?

cueCard.topic: Describe an achievement you are proud of.
cueCard.explain: and explain why you are proud of this achievement.

questions.text: Describe an achievement you are proud of.
questions.say: Thank you. Now, in Part 2, I'm going to give you a topic, and I'd like you to talk about it for one to two minutes. Before you talk, you'll have one minute to think about what you're going to say. You can make some notes if you wish. Here is your topic. Describe an achievement you are proud of. You should say: what you achieved; when it happened; how you achieved it; and explain why you are proud of this achievement.

questions.text: Did anyone help you to achieve this?
questions.say: Thank you. Did anyone help you to achieve this?

questions.text: What kinds of achievements are most admired in your country?
questions.say: Thank you. We've been talking about an achievement you are proud of, and I'd like to discuss with you some more general questions related to this. Let's consider first of all achievement. What kinds of achievements are most admired in your country?

questions.text: Is it more important to work hard or to be talented?
questions.say: Is it more important to work hard or to be talented?

questions.text: Why do some people give up when things become difficult?
questions.say: Why do some people give up when things become difficult?

questions.text: Should people be rewarded for their achievements at school or at work?
questions.say: Now let's talk about recognition. Should people be rewarded for their achievements at school or at work?

questions.text: Is money the best way to reward people for good work?
questions.say: Is money the best way to reward people for good work?

questions.text: Why do some people who achieve great things never become famous?
questions.say: Why do some people who achieve great things never become famous?
